properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED AS ARCHITECTURE, and this one is a DELIBERATE chokepoint rather than merely an unavoidable one. A session names the design it works on through exactly one door, and `registry.rs` says why in its own words: `Registry::attach` takes an id and treats it as an ID ALWAYS, there is deliberately no `path_for(id)` and no `attach_path`, because "a convenience overload is exactly how this property would be lost, so it is absent rather than documented".

⭐ SO REDUNDANCY HERE WOULD BE A DEFECT, not a repair. The property `ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design` protects — that a session cannot reach a design it was not attached to — holds BY CONSTRUCTION precisely because there is one route in. A second path is the thing that guarantee exists to forbid.

⚠️ NOT ACCEPTED: that concentration carries no risk. If this door breaks, every session is affected. What is accepted is that the concentration is the security property, and that `add_redundancy` would trade a correctness guarantee for an availability one nobody has asked for.
